cluster_summary: Multiple CVEs in this cluster involve parsing user-controlled structured data (YAML, JSON, binary) without enforcing a maximum nesting depth or recursion limit, allowing attackers to craft deeply nested inputs that cause stack overflow or resource exhaustion. The vulnerabilities span different parsers and data formats but share a common root of missing depth checks.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled binary length fields, size counters, frame lengths, offsets, back-references, or decompressed-size metadata into memory allocation, buffer growth, parsing loops, frame handling, decompression, or resource-consuming work. Report code paths where protocol-specific upper bounds, arithmetic overflow checks, structural consistency checks, or expansion limits are absent before allocation or work expansion. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should enforce explicit size limits, validate arithmetic and offsets before use, reject malformed or oversized records early, and bound decompression or frame-processing work.

mechanism.missing_guard: protocol-specific upper bounds, arithmetic overflow checks, structural consistency checks, or expansion limits are absent before allocation or work expansion
mechanism.name: unbounded binary length or size field drives resource use
mechanism.sink_shape: memory allocation, buffer growth, parsing loops, frame handling, decompression, or resource-consuming work
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled binary length fields, size counters, frame lengths, offsets, back-references, or decompressed-size metadata
mechanism.typical_fix: enforce explicit size limits, validate arithmetic and offsets before use, reject malformed or oversized records early, and bound decompression or frame-processing work

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Check for the next token being START_ARRAY before recursing, and throw an exception if a nested array is detected.
sub_patterns.name: Missing nested array detection in JSON single-value array unwrapping
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code assumes that when UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS is enabled, only a single wrapping array will be encountered, but it does not check for nested arrays before recursively calling deserialize, leading to unbounded recursion.
